summary: A paper on the problems of serving remote users on the ARPANET. The author says that after host unavailability, the most vexing issue was poor administrative procedure and information for remote users. Procedures that work for local users may fail for off-site ones, and the paper proposes solutions.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC argues that remote users need clear information about service hosts. It proposes a common outline for account procedures, documentation, technical details and operating practices.

how to support remote arpanet users
what information do remote users need

subtitle: Suggestions for helping remote users find information and support at service hosts.

tldr.problem: Administrative procedures and information that worked for local users often did not serve remote ARPANET users well.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC proposes an outline and questionnaire covering accounts, documentation, assistance, technical capabilities and operations.
tldr.outcome: It recommends organizing existing information in a consistent format so users can find it across host sites.

sections.title: Why Remote Users Need More Information
sections.content:
The author says that, after host unavailability, inadequate administrative procedures and information were among the most vexing problems for people trying to use network service hosts. Local users may rely on informal procedures that remote users cannot learn easily.

The Resource Notebook and documents collected by the NIC provide useful information, but the author says remote users may have trouble discovering the documents and cannot keep loaned copies for reference.
sections.plainLanguage: Local users can learn unwritten procedures from people nearby. Remote users need that information written down and easy to find.

sections.title: Information the Outline Covers
sections.content:
The proposed outline asks how users open and monitor service accounts, obtain documents and updates, contact support, and learn about login procedures, command languages, file systems and programming languages.

It also asks about security, output and storage services, operating schedules, charges, service availability and communication with operations staff. The author presents these as questions for documentation rather than requirements for a particular host.
sections.plainLanguage: The outline covers practical questions a remote user may have, from opening an account to getting help. It also asks how each host handles files, programs, costs and operating hours.

sections.title: A Consistent Guide to Existing Documents
sections.content:
The author recognizes that rewriting all host documentation could duplicate work and create extra maintenance. One option is to create a guide to each site's existing literature, organized according to the proposed outline.

A common format could help a user find comparable information across multiple hosts while letting each site maintain its own procedures and documents.
sections.plainLanguage: A host does not need to rewrite every manual. It can list its existing documents under common headings so remote users can find them more easily.
